Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds (3 element(s))
findings.severity_reason: High because WCAG 2.2 AA (a legal requirement under the 2018 Accessibility Regulations) sets a 4.5:1 minimum contrast ratio; this page fails it on 3 elements, including the privacy policy link.
findings.evidence: Motorlog · Privacy Policy ·
findings.regulation: WCAG 2.2 AA (Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations 2018)
findings.fix: Increase the contrast between text and background to at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).

findings.title: Buttons must have discernible text (1 element(s))
findings.severity_reason: Critical because WCAG 2.2 AA success criterion 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) requires every control to have an accessible name — an unnamed button is a direct, unambiguous breach of the 2018 Accessibility Regulations.
findings.evidence: <button class="w-9 h-9 flex items-center justify-center bg-[#141414] rounded-xl border border-[#222222] text-[#888888] hover:text-white hover:border-[#444444] transition-colors">
findings.regulation: WCAG 2.2 AA (Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations 2018)
findings.fix: Give icon-only buttons an accessible name, e.g. aria-label="Open menu".

findings.title: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds (4 element(s))
findings.severity_reason: High because it breaches the same WCAG 2.2 AA contrast requirement on 4 elements, including the contact email required by UK GDPR Art. 13(1)(a).
findings.evidence: Questions? privacy@motorlog.app
findings.regulation: WCAG 2.2 AA (Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations 2018)
findings.fix: Increase the contrast between text and background to at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy header
findings.severity_reason: Medium because UK GDPR Art. 32 requires 'appropriate technical measures' to secure personal data; a missing CSP is a gap against that standard, independent of whether an exploit has occurred.
findings.fix: Add a Content-Security-Policy header that only allows scripts from your own domain and trusted sources, e.g. default-src 'self'. Start in Report-Only mode to test it.

findings.title: No clickjacking protection (X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors)
findings.severity_reason: Medium because this also falls under the Art. 32 duty to secure personal data against unauthorised access — a lower-risk gap here, but a compliance gap regardless.
findings.fix: Add Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' (or X-Frame-Options: DENY) so other sites can't embed yours in a frame.

findings.title: Privacy notice doesn't say who the data controller is
findings.severity_reason: High because UK GDPR Art. 13(1)(a) makes this mandatory, not optional — without it, people have no one to direct a data request or complaint to.
findings.evidence: our trained classifier found no sentence covering this
findings.fix: State the legal name and address of the organisation (or person) responsible for the data, e.g. 'Example Ltd, 1 High Street, London, is the data controller.'
